speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; tell me, exactly how many days old are you when these symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Jejunal Atresia.

I see you are only six hours old with bilious vomiting and a brother with pyloric stenosis; however, the timing and bilious nature strongly suggest a distal obstruction like atresia rather than pyloric stenosis. Can you tell me if there is a palpable abdominal mass or if you noticed any polyhydramnios during your pregnancy?
